Abstract
Highlights
What are the main findings?
Effective CAV controllability depends on spatial availability, HDV response, platoon organization, and information and computation quality—not on penetration alone.
Cross-scale resilience requires coupling vehicle/platoon actuation with signal, routing, and regional traffic control while evaluating service retention, cumulative loss, and recovery time.
What are the implications of the main findings?
V2X quality should be treated as a control constraint that triggers graded cooperation, safe fallback, and re-synchronization rather than as an ideal communication assumption.
Deployment evidence should progress from simulation to real-data, SIL/HIL, and field validation under reproducible physical and communication disturbances.
Abstract
Connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) are emerging as mobile sensing and actuation resources in mixed traffic, but their contribution to urban road-network resilience depends on more than nominal penetration. An auditable pre-submission update retrieved 1601 raw records from the Web of Science Core Collection, ScienceDirect, and IEEE Xplore and yielded 1476 unique auditable candidates after deduplication. 9.7. Limitations of the Review
This review has seven principal limitations. First, it is a structured critical review rather than a registered systematic review; the 2026 WoS/ScienceDirect/IEEE update is auditable, but early database-by-database Scopus/TRID logs cannot be reconstructed fully, so exhaustive coverage is not claimed. The original review workflow did not employ dual independent screening or a prospectively defined inter-reviewer agreement protocol; consequently, formal Cohen’s
κ
statistics are not reported. Borderline records were resolved through author discussion, but some judgment remains unavoidable in a structured critical review. Similarly, the E0–E4 ladder is used as a qualitative interpretation framework rather than an exhaustive numerical classification of all records, and the CiteSpace modularity/silhouette values are descriptive network diagnostics without null-model significance testing. Second, simulation platforms, demand, penetration, disturbance design, baselines, and metrics vary substantially, making reported percentage improvements non-comparable. Third, much of the evidence remains E0–E2 despite increasing real-data, testbed, HIL, and engineering-platform work; evidence on E3–E4 urban-network resilience remains scarce. Fourth, the E0–E4 scale and the control-quality contract are author-defined synthesis tools and have not been externally standardized. Fifth, the 268-record candidate list contains sufficient bibliographic information for year, venue, and author-frequency summaries but not complete affiliation or citation metadata; conse

10. Conclusions
The reviewed evidence indicates that CAV penetration should be interpreted as potential rather than automatically realized control authority. The strongest evidence currently concerns mixed-platoon stabilization, vehicle-level disturbance attenuation, and intersection/corridor efficiency. Network-level resilience additionally depends on where controllable vehicles are located, what traffic and infrastructure states remain observable, how HDVs respond, whether communication and computation support the intended cooperation mode, and whether local actions are coordinated with signal, routing, perimeter, and residual-capacity control.
The literature is considerably less mature for closed-loop network recovery under simultaneous physical and information-layer disturbances. Self-sensing UHPC illustrates a possible additional infrastructure-state sensing layer, but the reviewed material studies do not yet demonstrate a complete material-signal–traffic-control–network-recovery loop. It is therefore treated as a prospective observability interface rather than established evidence of resilience improvement.
Accordingly, the effective-controllability indicators, communication-aware control-quality contract, and E0–E4 evidence ladder proposed in this review should be interpreted as author-defined synthesis tools rather than externally validated standards. {"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=adaptive+risk+sensitivity+parameters+in+reinforcement+learning+and+MPC+for+long-term+preference+stability&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"Resilient Cooperative Control of Connected and Automated Mixed Traffic: From Effective Controllability to Network Recovery\", \"abstract\": null, \"doi\": null, \"pmid\": \"PMC13667526\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13667526\", \"source\": \"PMC\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"PubMedCentral\", \"url\": \"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13667526/?tool=EBI\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"PubMedCentral\", \"url\": \"https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13667526/pdf/?tool=EBI\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13667526\"}, {\"availability\": \"Free\", \"availabilityCode\": \"F\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13667526?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Data-Driven and Physics-Informed Modeling Perspectives for Soft Manipulators: From SINDy to Hybrid Intelligence.\", \"abstract\": \"Soft manipulators offer a route to safer, more adaptive and physically intelligent robots, but their compliant bodies remain difficult to model, predict and control. Large deformation, distributed actuation, hysteresis, material variability and contact-rich interaction challenge both classical mechanics-based models and purely data-driven approaches. Here, we examine emerging modeling perspectives for soft manipulators through a conceptual progression from sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics to hybrid intelligence. We discuss how sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics (SINDy), Koopman learning, neural ordinary differential equations, physics-informed neural networks, and hybrid physics machine learning models contribute complementary capabilities, including interpretable reduced-order dynamics, control-ready prediction, continuous-time latent modeling, physics-constrained field reconstruction, and residual correction. We present that no single modeling approach is sufficient for the next generation of soft robotic systems. Instead, progress requires integrated modeling ecosystems that combine mechanical structure, data-driven discovery and task-aware adaptation. Such hybrid-intelligence frameworks can transform models from passive descriptions of deformation into active components of sensing, control, design and decision-making, enabling soft manipulators that are more interpretable, robust and deployable in real-world environments.\", \"doi\": \"10.1002/advs.78334\", \"pmid\": \"42893451\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13677003\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.78334\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13677003\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13677003?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"PPO-GAT-Follow: Graph-Attention Reinforcement Learning for Robust Robot Person Following in Dense Crowds.\", \"abstract\": \"Robot person following (RPF) in dense crowds requires a mobile robot to maintain an appropriate relative position with respect to a moving target while avoiding surrounding pedestrians and satisfying rear-following and social constraints. This paper proposes PPO-GAT-Follow, an interaction-aware reinforcement learning framework for dense-crowd RPF under geometric visibility loss with available target-relative pose estimates. The follower, target pedestrian, and surrounding pedestrians are represented as graph nodes, and a graph attention encoder models their local interactions. A task-oriented reward mechanism jointly accounts for target maintenance, visibility preservation, collision avoidance, proximity-aware social compliance, rear position maintenance, post-arrival stabilization, and action stability. Experiments are conducted in IR-SIM under fixed-route and random-route settings, with comparisons against MPC, DWA, SFM, and an adapted SARL baseline. In the fixed-route setting with 12 background pedestrians, PPO-GAT-Follow achieves a task success rate of 98.8% and a collision rate of 1.1%, improving task success by 10.9 percentage points over MPC. In the random-route setting at the training density, it achieves 83.1% task success and an SPL of 0.815, outperforming MPC by 18.3 percentage points in task success; at this density, it also surpasses SARL in the main task-level metrics. Zero-shot evaluations across crowd densities, together with structural and reward ablations, reward weight sensitivity analysis, tolerance shift tests, multi-seed training, and stress testing under target pose noise and heterogeneous pedestrian dynamics, further demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed framework. Gazebo-based validation also demonstrates system integration feasibility with localization, point cloud-based surrounding pedestrian perception, tracking, and UWB-like target-relative pose input. Nevertheless, visual target identification, re-identification, and perception-level occlusion recovery remain outside the scope of the present validation.\", \"doi\": \"10.3390/s26154711\", \"pmid\": \"42590488\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13468753\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3390/s26154711\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13468753\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13468753?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Application of Artificial Intelligence in Aquaculture, Processing, Safety, and Traceability in the Industry of Aquatic Products: A Review.\", \"abstract\": \"The aquatic products industry has experienced rapid development due to the growing global demand for high-quality proteins. However, conventional production models remain constrained by multifaceted impediments, including disease outbreaks, environmental stressors, microbial contamination, and operational inefficiencies in processing, quality control, and logistics. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers targeted methodological solutions to these challenges. From a functional perspective, this review categorizes artificial intelligence into four major types: perception, prediction, control, and generation, and systematically evaluates its application progress in aquaculture, processing, quality inspection, and traceability fields. Perception AI constitutes the data acquisition and digitization layer, utilizing computer vision, sonar, and multimodal fusion technologies to establish digital mappings from environmental parameters to biological indicators. Prediction AI employs machine learning and deep learning algorithms to transform historical datasets into quantitative forecasts regarding water quality dynamics, disease risks, and production trends. Control AI translates decision-making protocols into precise, autonomous regulatory actions for aquaculture environments and processing workflows through fuzzy logic and model-based predictive control. Generation AI leverages large language models and generative adversarial networks to demonstrate innovative capabilities in data augmentation, solution optimization, and virtual simulation. claims.statement: State reconstruction in WAKE is strictly deterministic, relying on replay of accepted operations rather than a mutable state cache.

support.explanation: This confirms the rejection of mutable state caches in favor of event-based reconstruction.
support.passage: Current state is never trusted as a separate cache. ``replay`` starts from an empty mapping, verifies every event in sequence, and applies only accepted operations.

claims.statement: The governance module enforces state validity by rejecting invalid proposals before they are appended to the durable record.

support.explanation: This establishes the separation of concerns: proposals are model-generated, validation is governance-enforced.
support.passage: The model is allowed to PROPOSE changes to durable state. It is never allowed to decide whether those changes are valid.
